business_problem: Comcast's cybersecurity teams depended on multiple siloed security analytics tools that did not elastically scale or give threat hunters, compliance teams, and business units a shared, current view of security data.
solution_summary: Comcast made Snowflake the core of a cloud-native security data fabric so cybersecurity, compliance, data science, and executive teams could work from common records instead of siloed tools. Security telemetry from multiple sources is joined, cleaned, and written into a common schema in Snowflake, where the platform holds 10 PB of data with over a year of hot retention for threat hunting and controls assurance. That shared lake lets threat hunters search petabyte-scale history, supports time-series ML for threat detection, and feeds dashboards that expose KPIs, KRIs, and compliance posture to business units in near real time. The architecture also enabled sweeps of more than 50,000 indicators of compromise across the 10-PB lake in under 30 minutes and helped one business unit raise endpoint-detection coverage to 95% in three days. By giving every stakeholder access to the same governed security data, Comcast reduced false positives and built a more proactive compliance culture.
